card.name: Small words before places or subjects
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as in, of, at, to study, or live, right after a noun like convent, muse, or court in historical, religious, or arts writing. The next word is usually a place or a field of study.

modes.label: Linking word after institution or muse
modes.description: A preposition such as in, of, or at follows a noun like convent, muse, or court and is followed by a place or art.
modes.example: Terpsichore: Terpsichore was initially the muse of Dance – her name means the one that likes to dance – and also the muse<< of>> Lyric Poetry.

modes.label: Verb before a setting or subject
modes.description: A verb such as live or study sits before a place or an academic subject.
modes.example: Lawrence won a scholarship to Jesus College, Cambridge, to<< study>> History.

card.plain: It fires on small linking words in history and arts text that come just before a place or a field of study.
